name: M2 -> the zero pad is narrowed from two digits to one inside the single owner. The carry is still correct, so no clock ever reads :60, and the defect is invisible on every value whose seconds limb is ten or more. Only single-digit seconds lose their leading zero: 8:00 becomes 8:0 and 0:07 becomes 0:7. This is the shape of a well-formedness gate that tested only the ceiling and never the width
note: NAMED TRIP: C2 rows _clkMS(0) == '0:00', _clkMS(7) == '0:07', _clkMS(59.5) == '1:00', _clkMS(299.5) == '5:00', _clkMS(479.6) == '8:00', _clkMS(480) == '8:00', _clkMS(3600) == '60:00' and _clkMS(3660) == '61:00' go red, each printing a one-character seconds limb. C3 goes red naming 0 -> 0:0 first, under the 'two digit seconds limb' clause rather than the 00..59 clause. C4 goes red because the helper no longer matches the idiom on the 11,901 inputs where the idiom was correct. C5's 'prints the tempo pace as 8:00/mi' goes red while C5's ':60 limb' row stays GREEN, which is exactly what separates a width defect from a carry defect. C6 goes red. STAYING GREEN: C2 rows with a two-digit seconds limb (59, 59.4, 61.5, 450.6, 479.4, 518.4, 570, 689.7, 3599), C4b, C5 dose.tgt == 480, and the HALF_MANNY digest row, since run_half prints no affected string.

name: M3 -> _fmtPace is re-pointed away from the single owner and back to the inline idiom it had on V203. The helper survives untouched and still passes its own hand table, so D126's helper looks perfectly healthy; the callers are simply not using it. This is the regression a future rename or merge would actually produce, and the reason the gate cross-checks a rendered card against dose.tgt instead of only unit-testing the helper
anchor: const _fmtPace = s => _clkMS(s) + '/mi';   // D126 (V204): seconds limb owned by _clkMS
note: NAMED TRIP: C5 'W11 THU detail prints the tempo pace as 8:00/mi' and C5 'W11 THU detail carries no :60 seconds limb' both go red, printing Mario's original '3 x 20 min at Tempo Pace: 7:60/mi'. C6 goes red naming the mile anchor, week and day of each card whose printed clock disagrees with the clock the gate computed from dose.tgt. DISCRIMINATING: C1, every C2 row, C3, C4 and C4b must ALL STAY GREEN, because the helper itself is not touched. That green-helper / red-card split is the whole discrimination of this mutation: it proves C5 and C6 test the wiring and not the arithmetic, and that a passing unit table is not evidence the app uses it. C5's dose.tgt == 480 row stays green: the number never depended on the formatter. The HALF_MANNY digest row stays green.

name: M6 -> the same revert as M1, inside _clkMS itself, but judged by g202_int_doctrine.js instead of g204_clock_limb.js. This is the mutation the slice-7 lattice row makes possible: on V203 this gate could not see this defect at all, because no config it built reached a goal pace that carries across the minute. With the 6:46 mile at seed 76308 in the lattice it can. A survivor here would mean the coverage gap D126 names is still open in the doctrine gate

note: NAMED TRIP: D10b ('every clock printed on all N INT cards of the 6:46 mile / seed 76308 config has a two-digit seconds limb in 00..59'), D10c (the carry is no longer reached, because the goal pace now prints 6:60 rather than 7:00), D10d (the reproducing card no longer prints the hand-computed 7:00/mi) and D3 (the card prints neither the goal-pace sentence nor the cutback sentence, because the tightened parser refuses 6:60). Note the SHAPE of the failure: it surfaces as a malformed-pace failure, not as wrong arithmetic. The numbers were never wrong; the string was. D1, D2, D4, D5, D7, D8 and D9 must STAY GREEN, because every other lattice point sits a whole second from the minute and the two formatters agree there. D7's pinned PRT TING grid staying green is the specific proof that this mutation is discriminating rather than broad.
deviation: The ruling asked for M6 to revert one tightened seconds limb inside tests/gates/g202_int_doctrine.js itself. tests/sabotage.py cannot express that: it reads `src` from the CANDIDATE ARTIFACT only (sabotage.py main(), `src = open(cand).read()`), mutates that string, and runs an UNMUTATED gate against it. A mutation is therefore always a mutation of index.html. M6 keeps the ruling's intent - prove that the slice-7 lattice row turned g202_int_doctrine.js into a gate that can fail on the defect D126 names - by pointing the SAME defect at THIS gate. The gate's own regex tightness is instead made load-bearing behaviourally by D10a, which asserts the line-131 parser rejects the literal '6:60' and accepts '7:00'; loosening [0-5]\d to \d\d there reds D10a on any artifact.
